newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN BONDS EASE IN RESPONSE TO U.S. MARKET.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BONDS EASE IN RESPONSE TO U.S. MARKET.

text.p: FUTURES CASH YIELD
* Long-dated local yields continue to rise after U.S Treasuries pressured by 30-year bond refunding auction.
* Locally, June housing finance falls, but within range and no further talk of yet another easing.
Australian long bond yields continued to rise in response to a weakening U.S. Treasuries market which came under pressure from the 30-year bond quarterly refunding auction.
The U.S. long bond yield ended five basis points higher at 6.53 percent, with local dealers expecting further price falls when the U.S. local market reopens for Friday's session.

Dealers said the local September 10-year bond futures contract faced further pressure in late morning trade in response to the U.S. market, but entirely overlooked June housing finance data issued at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Housing finance by volume fell 2.1 percent in June, a result which was within expectations.
The September 10-year local contract fell to 93.430, easing from 93.470 earlier in the session and the 93.600 high touched overnight in after-hours trading.
"Once the market broke that 93.47/49 level you saw some people getting out of the market," one Sydney dealer said.
"A few got out of the market today given the very poor performance in the States last night. And people are probably expecting further weakness in the U.S. overnight," he said.
The lack of major local data next week meant that the U.S. would dictate direction for some time, one dealer said.

Speculation about yet another local rate cut continued to focus the minds of some traders watching shorter-dated securities, an outcome that would have won more credibility if the June housing finance data had been much lower.
The 90-day bill futures contract was steady at 95.10 and the yield on the ruling three-year contract was only one tick higher than the morning start at 5.57 percent.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
